2_Introduction: By interlinking experimental conditions with device architecture, a perovskite solar cell was fabricated, affirming a PCE of 23.9518%, FF of 84.9684%, Voc of 1.126 V, and Jsc of 25.034 mA/cm². For the perovskite film, 1.73 mol/L precursor solution was prepared according to the chemical formula of Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0. The perovskite film was deposited by spin-coating onto the substrate using a two-step spin-coating process, first at 1000 rpm for 10 s and then at 5000 rpm for 40 s. A timed antisolvent drop (160 µL at last 10 s) enhanced the perovskite crystallization kinetics. After the whole spin-coating process, the substrate was annealed at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The perovskite layer, formulated as Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀, leverages a carefully tuned A-site cation mixture to optimize the Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98), thereby stabilizing the photoactive α-phase while suppressing δ-phase nucleation and mitigating halide segregation and volatile MA⁺ loss; the precise precursor concentration (1.73 mol/L) governs supersaturation during spin-coating, where the two-step protocol—initial low-speed (1000 rpm, 10 s) spreading followed by high-speed (5000 rpm, 40 s) crystallization—enables controlled solvent evaporation kinetics, and the precisely timed antisolvent quench (160 µL delivered at the final 10 s) triggers instantaneous nucleation by rapidly extracting DMF/DMSO, yielding dense, pinhole-free films with enlarged grain domains and reduced grain boundary density—this crystallization control directly suppresses undercoordinated Pb²⁺ and I⁻ vacancies at surfaces and interfaces, minimizing non-radiative recombination centers and enhancing carrier diffusion length; although no exogenous SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in this formulation, the intrinsic defect tolerance of the mixed-cation composition synergizes with the kinetic crystallization window to promote self-passivation—Cs⁺ enhances lattice rigidity and reduces thermal disorder, FA⁺ provides optimal octahedral tilting stability and deep valence band maximum, while trace MA⁺ improves interfacial wettability and transient dipole screening during nucleation; critically, the absence of extrinsic passivators places full reliance on process-engineered structural integrity, as corroborated by implicit morphological evidence embedded in the high-performance metrics—namely, the exceptional FF of 84.9684% reflects minimal series resistance and highly uniform charge extraction, the Voc of 1.126 V indicates suppressed interfacial recombination and low trap-assisted Shockley–Read–Hall losses, and the Jsc of 25.034 mA/cm² confirms near-complete photon harvesting and efficient carrier collection across the film—collectively, these performance parameters—Voc of 1.126 V, Jsc of 25.034 mA/cm², FF of 84.9684%, and PCE of 23.9518%—demonstrate that thermodynamically stabilized cation engineering, coupled with kinetically optimized crystallization, achieves defect-minimized electronic quality without molecular intervention.
